summary: Willy Foy was an indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig (1892-1895), studying under Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann. He directed the Rautenstrauch-Joest Museum (1901-1925) and taught at the University of Cologne (1914; 1920-1929).
Indologist Willy Zinkgräf studied under Max Walleser in 1922 and completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University by 1939. He later held a post at the Walleser-Institut.

Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who completed his degrees at Leiden University, earning his doctorate under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (1970-1974). He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976-1999) and Harvard University (2000-2013).

Winfred P. Lehmann was a linguist and indologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1938-1941). He later served as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986-2007).
Winfred Robert Martin was a linguist and indologist. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and later worked as a librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winfried Petri was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. under Helmut Hoffmann at the University of Munich by 1966, later serving there as apl. Professor (1971) and director (1977-1979).

Wing-tsit Chan was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Harvard University (~1924-1929). He held faculty posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1935-1942), Dartmouth College (~1942-1966), and Chatham University (~1966-1982).

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan studied at Cornell and earned a J.D. and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at Washington and Lee, Chicago, the University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Winston Kyan is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago, where he studied under Linda Seidel and doctoral supervisor Hung Wu.

Winston L. King was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard (~1938-1940). He held professorial posts at Grinnell College (1949-1964), Vanderbilt University (1964-1973), and Colorado State University (1973-1975).

Wladimir Zwalf was an indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied under Thomas Burrow at Lincoln College (1952-1955) and served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1957-1962) and the British Museum (1962-1993).

Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and japanology who studied at Columbia University and Harvard. He spent his career at Columbia University (1953-2017) as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies.

Wojciech Marceli Gielecki was an indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. at Jagiellonian University (~1896-1901). He subsequently worked as a librarian at Jagiellonian University from around 1901 to 1939.

Wolfgang Adolf Theilkuhl was an indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg (1919-1920) and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Munich (1918-1926). He served as a lecturer at King's College London (1828-1833).

Wolfgang Franke was a sinologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg. He taught at Peking and Sichuan Universities and held the sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950-1977).

Wolfgang Krause was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen (~1919-1921). He served as Professor of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Königsberg (1929-1937) and the University of Göttingen (1937-1963).

Wolfgang Lentz worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at Göttingen (~1920-1923). He worked at the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1924-1942) and was later a professor at the University of Hamburg (1955-1968).

Indologist and linguist Wolfgang Morgenroth earned his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild. He served as professor at the University of Greifswald (1969-1972) and later as Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972-1994).
Wolfgang Schlüter was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu (~1867-1874) under Leo Meyer. He later held an academic post at the University of Tartu from around 1877 to 1914.

Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1900-1904). He served at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918-1921) and as Professor and Chair of Philosophy at Munich (1934).
